books.section: Topic 7.4 The Progressives — The Progressive Movement, Race, and Segregation
The Progressive Era and World War I (1900-1920)

stimulus.source_note: Paraphrase of Barron's Premium 2027, Chapter 9, and 5 Steps to a 5 2024, Chapter 20.
stimulus.text: Paraphrase of Barron's Premium 2027, Chapter 9, and 5 Steps to a 5 2024, Chapter 20: Most white Progressives accepted the segregation of the Jim Crow South and did little for Black Americans. President Woodrow Wilson allowed his cabinet to resegregate federal offices, and he praised the film Birth of a Nation (1915). Black reformers organized for themselves: W. E. B. Du Bois helped found the National Association for the Advancement of Colored People (NAACP) in 1909 to demand full equality. Black women pursued the same reforms as white women, temperance, education, and uplift, but their work left few written records and stayed nearly invisible in histories of the movement. Women's suffrage, organized since the National American Woman Suffrage Association formed in 1890, finally won the Nineteenth Amendment in 1920.

source: original; stimulus paraphrased from 5 Steps to a 5 2024, Chapter 20, and Barron's Premium 2027, Chapter 9
stem: The passage best supports which conclusion about Progressivism and race?

options.text: Progressives ended Jim Crow in the South entirely
options.misconception: Jim Crow survived the Progressive Era; most white Progressives accepted segregation.

options.text: Wilson desegregated the federal government offices
options.misconception: Wilson did the opposite: his administration resegregated federal offices.

options.text: the NAACP was founded by white Progressives alone, without Black help
options.misconception: The NAACP was founded by Black and white reformers together, with Du Bois among its founders.

options.text: most Progressives accepted segregation, and Black reformers had to organize for themselves

rationales.A: Jim Crow outlasted the Progressive Era. The passage says most white Progressives accepted segregation.
rationales.B: Wilson resegregated federal offices. Desegregation is the opposite of what his administration did.
rationales.C: Du Bois, a Black scholar and activist, helped found the NAACP alongside white reformers. It was not a white-only project.
rationales.D: The passage shows white Progressives accepting segregation, Wilson resegregating federal offices, and Black reformers answering by founding the NAACP and pursuing reform on their own terms. The movement's limits forced self-organization.
rationales.general:
1. Gather the passage's evidence. Most white Progressives accepted segregation, Wilson resegregated offices and praised Birth of a Nation, and the NAACP was founded by Black reformers.
2. Add it up. The movement that promised reform left Black Americans to organize for themselves.
3. Rule out the reversals. Jim Crow did not end, Wilson did not desegregate, and the NAACP was not a white-only project.
Remember: a movement's limits show in whom it leaves out, so ask who had to organize without its help.
